title: Support Garden: runbooklet harvester and privileged admin toolkit
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a lightweight, composable 'runbooklet' runtime (Support Garden) plus a privileged admin toolkit that lets SREs and support engineers author, schedule, and harvest small runbook tasks. The goal is to reduce mean time to resolution for common incidents by providing audited, idempotent building blocks (runbooklets) that can be composed into automation flows or executed ad-hoc via CLI/Console. This ticket covers the runtime, a CLI shim for safe execution, and the audit/telemetry hooks needed for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Runbooklet authoring: engineers can create a runbooklet manifest (YAML/JSON) with inputs, outputs, and a dry-run mode
Idempotency: repeated executions with same inputs must not produce side effects (or must be explicitly marked non-idempotent)
RBAC & gating: toolkit honors RBAC roles and integrates with SSO; privileged steps require approval if run from Console
Audit trail: every execution (dry-run or live) writes a structured event to the audit-log service and links to the Console trace
Scheduler: runbooklets can be scheduled by name and harvested by the harvester service with retry/backoff and safe concurrency limits
Observability: per-run telemetry (latency, success/fail, token cost) surfaced on a Support Garden dashboard and traced in request logs
Test coverage: unit + e2e tests for runtime, CLI, and the harvester with simulated RBAC and vault-backed secrets
Security review: security sign-off obtained and KMS/HSM integration pattern documented
tasks: Design runbooklet manifest schema and CLI UX (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Support+Garden+Runbooklet+Spec)
Implement lightweight runtime library (Go) for safe step execution and idempotency markers
CLI shim: support-garden cli with dry-run, preview, and approve flows (GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/support-garden/pull/214)
Harvester service: scheduler + worker pool with rate limits and audit-emitter
Integrate RBAC and check-guidance with SSO (AuthN/AuthZ) and feature-flag gate
Telemetry: emit prom metrics + structured events to audit-log; build Grafana dashboard (dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/support-garden)
End-to-end tests with ephemeral infra using staging-runbooklets (CI job: support-garden/e2e)
Security review and KMS pattern doc (Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops/security/support-garden-kms.pdf)
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for INC-2025-01 recommended small, audited runbooks for common remediation steps.
2025-02-13 Carlos Martinez: Spike completed—runtime prototype executes shell + API steps with a YAML manifest; initial idempotency token design implemented.
2025-02-15 Security review (first pass): flagged secret handling and suggested KMS envelope encryption; blocked privileged CLI commands until KMS integration is documented.
2025-02-16 PM review (Jules Tan): Suggested prioritizing dry-run UX and audit linking back to case IDs for support trackers.
2025-02-18 Carlos Martinez: Implemented audit events; pushed PR for CLI preview flow (PR #214). Added feature-flag gate (support_garden.enabled).

2025-02-20 Maya Patel: Decided to scope harvester to non-critical production maintenance tasks initially. For critical remediation we will require multi-approver flows. Recorded decision in Confluence.
2025-02-22 QA: Found race condition when two harvesters pick same scheduled job—added optimistic lock and exponential backoff. Updated acceptance criteria.
notes: Trade-offs: we could reuse the Ops Playbook runner (ENG-772005) but that runtime is heavy and not optimized for sub-minute runbooklets. Chose a lightweight Go runtime to reduce cold-start and make local dry-run easy.
Privilege model: favor read-only runbooklets by default; write-capable steps require signed approval token or Console approval flow.
Observability: link each runbooklet execution to Support Case ID to make regression detection easier in Optimize and Console rollouts.
Follow-ups: plan a separate ticket to add template-driven parameterization and a community-runbook store for on-call reuse.
